title: Spouse Amounts in a Replacement of Returned Disability Compensation
content:
**Clause.** The spouse addition in a replacement of a returned Disability Compensation payment is:

- the spouse addition plus the spouse aid-and-attendance addition, when a spouse is recorded on the award and the most recent spouse addition is marked as needing aid and attendance;
- the spouse addition alone, when a spouse is recorded and the most recent spouse addition is not so marked;
- nothing, when no spouse is recorded.

**Who is recorded.** The spouses that count are the spouse additions on the award less the spouse removals; every month a replacement covers counts the spouses so recorded. The most recent spouse addition is the one with the latest effective date.

**Which rates.** The amounts are those of the 100 percent tier — spouse addition 220.30, spouse aid-and-attendance addition 201.41 — when the award's decision history shows individual unemployability granted, and those of the award's own tier otherwise.

**Basis questions**

*The award shows one spouse addition and one spouse removal. Is a spouse recorded?* No: one addition less one removal leaves none, so the spouse amount is nothing.

*Two spouse additions are recorded and one removal; the later addition is marked as needing aid and attendance. What is added?* One spouse remains recorded and the most recent addition is so marked: the spouse addition plus the spouse aid-and-attendance addition. At Disability Compensation (60% Combined Rating) without individual unemployability that is 132.18 plus 120.85, that is 253.03 (hypothetical award).

*A spouse is recorded at Disability Compensation (80% Combined Rating) and the award's decision history shows individual unemployability granted; the spouse is not marked as needing aid and attendance. What is added?* The spouse addition of the 100 percent tier, 220.30 (hypothetical award).
